incident-bot: INCIDENT 2418002222 - High 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in eu-west-1. 5xx > 3% for 3m. PagerDuty triggered: @alex oncall. Alert links: https://alerts.redwood.internal/2418002222 :rotating_light:

alex: ack — oncall. I'm seeing 5xx spike starting ~2418000000. Pulling up DNS + LB healthchecks now.

alex: quick checks:
```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai A +short
52.16.10.5
3.120.45.7

$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai A +short
52.16.10.5
52.16.10.5

$ curl -sS -I https://52.16.10.5/v1/health | head -n1
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
```

alex: it looks like some resolvers are returning an old eu-west IP (52.16.10.5) that is currently degraded. Route53 health checks for eu-west show failing ~3m ago. Cloudfront/CF resolvers also returning mixed answers due to low TTL caches.

maya: reported by synthetic probes in eu-west-1 too. I'm opening Route53 console — possible Route53 geo routing weight skew or a misconfigured health check flapping. Will check CloudWatch alarms and recent DNS changes.

leo: pinging Cloudflare status + RIPE/other resolver networks. Cloudflare dashboard shows increased 5xx to our origin from eu edge pool, but CF edge itself not degraded. Might be origin connectivity.

alex: temporary mitigation plan:
- reduce DNS TTL to 60s for api.redwood.ai (to speed propagation)
- change geo DNS to direct eu traffic to fallback pool (eu-fallback) while we fix origin
- trigger CF cache purge for edge that serve inference static assets (not model weights)

alex: applying TTL change now:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123EXAMPLE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.120.45.7"}]}}]}'
```

maya: RFC: I'm seeing the change in the console. AWS reports status PENDING, propagation expected ~60s but resolver caching still possible. Opening a support case with R53 for healthcheck noise. Case #R53-241800.

leo: Cloudflare purged edge for zone ZONE123: `curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/ZONE123/purge_cache" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_TOKEN" --data '{"purge_everything":true}'` — confirmed 200.

alex: after TTL change + failover weight update, 5xx rate dropped from 3.8% -> 0.9% in last 2m. Still some clients hitting old answers.

pagerduty-bot: NOTE: Escalation threshold reached for incident 2418002222. Follow PD runbook for partial regional degradation.

samir: oncall shift starting in 10m — request handoff. Alex, can you summarize state + actions?

alex: summary for handoff:
- Impact: elevated 5xx for api.redwood.ai in eu-west-1; ~7% of total traffic affected at peak, now ~1%
- Root suspicion: Route53 geo-weight/healthcheck returned stale/degraded IP (52.16.10.5) leading to origin errors. Cloudflare returning mixed DNS answers due to cached low-TTL entries at some resolvers
- Actions taken: reduced TTL to 60s, updated Route53 to point eu traffic to eu-fallback pool (manual weight change), purged Cloudflare cache, opened R53 support case #R53-241800
- Current mitigations: traffic shifted to fallback pool, healthchecks for eu origin showing nominal. Monitoring: synthetic and traffic 5xx trending down.

samir: thanks. I'll take over. Next steps for me:
- keep R53 case open and get updates from AWS engineer
- monitor resolver-level 5xx and TTL propagation for next 30m
- prepare customer status update draft (see below)

leo: FYI I also kicked off a traceroute set from multiple public resolvers (ARIN probes) to track how widespread the stale answer is. Initial looks show EU ISP caches still returning old IPs for ~5-10 mins post-change.

samir: draft status to customers:
"We're investigating elevated error rates affecting inference API traffic in EU. We've rerouted traffic to a healthy fallback pool and implemented temporary DNS TTL/weight changes to accelerate recovery. We're monitoring performance and will provide another update in 30 minutes. No action needed on customer side."

maya: note for postmortem: capture why Route53 healthcheck flapped (network vs process), and add automated rollback threshold into RG policy so we can avoid manual weight swaps next time. Also capture CF resolver cache expiry behaviour and TTL recommendations for our endpoints.

samir: adding oncall next-step checklist to incident ticket. tagging @leo to keep running resolver probes + @alex for logs/metrics correlation. I'll be primary until 2418005444 then follow normal next-oncall.

alex: leaving thread for handoff, ping me if it resurfaces. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2418002222 — status changed to MONITORING. Updated at 2418005444.
